newsitem.title: UK: Yachtsman Bullimore's 15 minutes of fame fade fast.
newsitem.headline: Yachtsman Bullimore's 15 minutes of fame fade fast.

text.p: Yachtsman Tony Bullimores 15 minutes of fame were fading fast just days after his dramatic rescue, with three chocolate companies rejecting endorsement proposals and saying Bullimores story was past its sell-by date.

Mars, Cadbury Schweppes Plc and Nestle SA each said Bullimores British agent, Masters International, had proposed that for a fee of 20,000 pounds ($33,100) Bullimore would remember their product as the one that sustained him at sea.

The 56-year-old former Royal Marine, who was rescued on January 9 five days after his boat capsized in the icy Southern Ocean, had credited his survival to sheer determination, a little water and a little chocolate.
A spokesman for Masters International denied that agents had ever suggested misrepresenting the truth as part of any proposals put forth and denied that the firm had suggested a fee of 20,000 pounds.

A spokesman for Cadburys said the company was contacted by Bullimores agents on the day of his rescue. Initially we said we would look at some proposals, but our first concern was whether it was our product, the spokesman told Reuters.
As far as were concerned the story is well past its sell-by date, the spokesman added. Theres no longer any possibility of a deal. Theres also the question of credibility.
A spokesman for Mars said Bullimores agent contacted the confectionery company offering a deal for 20,000 pounds for Bullimore to remember a Mars product as the key to his survival at sea.

Nestle also said it rejected a similar proposal. They said Kit-Kat and Drifter had been involved in some way," a Nestle spokeswoman said. "We said we weren't interested and we've had no further contact.
"It's a bit late in the day to be doing anything," the Nestle spokeswoman added.
